conventions: A supplied English locative pro-adverb is folded onto the verb whose English it completes as a rule 7 helper and is not marked `added`: 'there' at 28:12 and 'hither' at 28:21. This holds even where the place expression the pro-adverb echoes is already spent on its own tokens in the same verse, as εἰς Συρακούσας is at 28:12. Rule 103's `added` arm was read as reaching full lexical content only, its own stated contrast naming a resumptive pronoun and rule 7's list ending in 'and similar words'. The competing reading is recorded in the 28:12 unit's note.

A concessive participle the ASV expands with the discontinuous frame 'though … yet' keeps that whole frame, the 'yet' included, in the participle's own unit under rules 15 and 86: διασωθέντα at 28:4 and ποιήσας at 28:17. Giving 'yet' to the main clause's finite verb as the word it introduces, or marking it `added` under rule 86, was considered and rejected in both verses — the participle is the token that carries the concession, and rule 27 forbids splitting the correlative from what licenses it. Both notes record the alternative.

Every supplied juncture 'and' at a seam the ASV creates by converting Greek participles into finite clauses is folded onto the constituent it introduces under rule 88: 28:2, 28:3, 28:5, 28:6, 28:7, 28:13, 28:14, 28:15 and 28:21. This includes 28:8, where the constituent introduced is itself a participle ('and laying'), on the reading that rule 98's `added` arm is scoped to a seam whose two constituents are rendered alike — at 28:8 the flanking participles are rendered finite and participial respectively, so neither rule 88's letter nor rule 98's reaches it and rule 88's principle decides. The chapter's only `added` juncture is the verse-initial 'And' of 28:13, which introduces no converted participle at all.
report: Read all 58 candidate groups and the dump end to end. Every multi-treatment bucket is ASV variation the source licenses or a difference of construction: δέ, καί, εἰς, πρός, λέγω, θηρίον, πυρά and οὐδείς follow whatever English word the ASV wrote, and the ὁ groups all resolve to rules 19/21 (aligned), rules 20/38/76 (determiner slot occupied, or a supplied possessive with no other word available to take it) or rule 23 (name, θεός, no determiner, second attributive article).

Four constructions checked closest, all consistent. Second attributive article: 28:2, 28:9, 28:17, 28:25 — unrepresented in all four, relativizer to the participle (rules 23, 31). Substantival article before a participle: 28:9 is emptied because the expressed οἱ λοιποί has already written the pronoun (rule 32's apposition clause), while 28:17 splits 'those'/'that were', 28:24 gives 'the things' (rules 22, 102) and 28:30 gives the single 'that' (rule 90) — the differences lie in the Greek and in the count of English words, not in the analysis.

πρῶτος: 28:7 τῷ πρώτῳ gives the article 'belonging to the … man' headed on 'man' (rule 102, unanimous in the corpus), and anarthrous πρώτους at 28:17 takes its own supplied 'the' (rules 51, 58). The same article test decides δευτεραῖοι at 28:13 and πλείονες at 28:23 on rule 17's anarthrous generic-noun clause. Rule 106 preverbs: the verb keeps its particle at 28:3, 28:5, 28:6, 28:8, 28:10, 28:13, 28:17, 28:19, 28:22, 28:27 and 28:30, and goes bare only at 28:16, where the expressed εἰς → 'into' already carries it.

The candidate table is blind to added units, so the supplied English was audited separately. Folded onto a licensing token: 'them' (28:3), 'their minds' (28:6), 'us' (28:7), 'board' (28:10), 'there' (28:12), 'our' (28:17), 'it' and 'whereof' (28:19), 'me' (28:20), 'hither' (28:21), 'the matter' (28:23), 'venomous' (28:4), 'none … him' (28:31). The chapter's one added unit is the verse-initial 'And' of 28:13, which introduces no converted participle and answers to no source token here or in a neighbouring verse. No verse folds a comparable unlicensed clause-initial connective, so there is no added-versus-folded split behind the clean table.

Head choices audited as a class: passive auxiliaries head on the lexical verb in all eight instances; support and resultative frames head on the meaning-bearing complement ('set sail'→sail 28:11, 'set me at liberty'→liberty 28:18, 'made a circuit'→circuit 28:13, 'is waxed gross'→gross 28:27); and the two recast privatives head on the stem word, not on the word spelling the prefix (ἀσύμφωνοι → 'agreed not' on 'agreed' 28:25, ἀκωλύτως → 'none forbidding him' on 'forbidding' 28:31). All follow rules 17, 84 and 91.

BSB disagreements: all seven are documented convention differences and none is an error. 28:2 τὴν and 28:10 τὰς have no English determiner at all (rules 20, 23); 28:3 τῆς is displaced by 'his' (rule 20); 28:7 τὸν by 'that' (rule 38); 28:9 οἱ is a second attributive article (rule 31); 28:15 ὁ stands before a name (rule 23); 28:5 μὲν is the report rule 70 says in terms is not a correction. Nothing was changed to improve the aggregate.

Verdict no-change: no patch, so no re-validation is needed. Three conventions recorded for judgments the chapter made more than once that the contract only implies; no promotion or amendment, since the two general lessons here (the locative pro-adverb fold and the participle-to-participle juncture) rest on this chapter alone and no corpus precedent was supplied for either.
